B2.title: Felix
B2.visualDescription: Vintage 35mm film camera resting on a darkroom wooden bench next to developed negatives.

pages.bio: I'm Felix. I shoot analog photos with a 35mm film camera. You only get 36 shots per roll and cannot check the photo immediately, so you have to be patient and focus on lighting and composition before developing negatives in the darkroom.
greenFlags: ✓ Real physical photo prints to keep
redFlags: ✗ Accidental light leaks can ruin photos

pages.bio: I convert my bathroom into a makeshift darkroom on Sunday afternoons. Mixing developer chemicals and watching silver-halide images emerge on photographic paper under red light is pure magic.
greenFlags: ✓ Master of classic analog darkroom chemistry

pages.bio: In an era of disposable digital media where people take thousands of forgotten smartphone photos, analog film forces you to slow down, respect light, and cherish single moments.
redFlags: ✗ Refuses to take quick selfie photos

B2.opener: Hi! Do you prefer taking fast photos on a smartphone or taking time with traditional film?
icebreakers: I like a bit of both!
B2.prompt: Compare smartphone photography with traditional film photography based on Felix's hobby.
